title: New class of exactly flat topological bands - compact localised states protected by local graph topology
abstract: Strongly correlated quantum matter is fundamentally defined by the tension between non-commuting quantum operators. Hamiltonians exhibiting macroscopic degeneracies are of general interest in this field because they imply an infinite susceptibility to any non-commuting perturbation. In moiré heterostructures, engineering such extensive degeneracies in the kinetic Hamiltonian creates a fertile garden for exotic strongly correlated phases of matter to emerge from the resulting flat bands. Here, we introduce a prescription to construct an infinite family of exact flat band Hamiltonians supported on the faces of arbitrary graphs. We demonstrate this algorithm on the faces of four Bravais lattices. Using a discrete graph generalization of the Atiyah-Singer index theorem, we prove that the extensive degeneracies of such face-graph Hamiltonians are protected by the local topology of the face-graph connectivity. The resulting macroscopic null spaces yield compact localised states that remain localised over time due to frustration in hopping pathways. We discuss the broad implications of such non-dispersing quantum modes in diverse settings, from arrested dynamics in quantum networks and quantum machine learning algorithms to Majorana-free topological quantum computation.
summary: This work introduces a general method to construct exact flat band Hamiltonians on the faces of any arbitrary graph. By linking the resulting extensive ground-state degeneracy to the local topology via graph index theorems, the authors prove that these macroscopic degeneracies are topologically protected. This has broad implications for designing quantum systems with robust, non-dispersing quantum modes.
main_problem: The primary goal is constructing an infinite family of exact flat band Hamiltonians supported on the faces of arbitrary graphs to study exotic strongly correlated phases.
main_result: The resulting extensive ground-state degeneracies are rigorously proven to be protected by the local topology of the face-graph connectivity, yielding compact localized states.
method: The construction uses a prescription based on the face-vertex incidence matrix (B) and generalizes concepts from the Atiyah-Singer index theorem via graph theory.
model_or_system: The model is built upon tight-binding Hamiltonians defined on the faces of arbitrary graphs, motivated by moiré heterostructures to engineer macroscopic degeneracies in quantum matter.
key_observables: Extensive ground-state degeneracy (scaling with $|F| - |V|$), compact localized states, and topological protection.
important_parameters: The hopping amplitudes ($t$) and the structure of the graph connectivity (faces $F$ vs. vertices $V$).
main_assumptions: The definition of a 'face' as an irreducible cycle is central to the construction; the analysis relies on the rank-nullity theorem applied to the incidence matrix.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate hopping processes (intra/inter-orbital) and show bandstructures for various lattices (cubic, hexagonal), demonstrating flat bands at specific energies.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by defining faces on graphs, deriving the Hamiltonian using the face-vertex incidence matrix B, calculating the null space dimension via rank-nullity, and finally proving topological protection using graph theory generalizations of index theorems.
why_interesting: The focus on engineered flat bands in moiré heterostructures directly relates to creating platforms for strongly correlated physics, which is a major area of interest in condensed matter theory.
